rejected.title: What gets researched
card: Research costs money, so choices are made about which projects get funded. Funding comes from governments, businesses, universities and charities.
Society's needs help steer those choices. A need might be cleaner energy or treatments for a common disease.
Society's values also help steer them. Values are beliefs about what matters, such as protecting the environment or caring for the sick.
So the topics that get funded can change over time. A problem that more people see as urgent is more likely to attract research money.
rejected.remember: What society needs and values helps steer which research gets funded.

a.q: Why is a lot of research money spent on ways to cut greenhouse gas emissions?
opts: Many people see climate change as a problem to solve
Other topics have already been fully explained
Science can only study problems linked to the air
Universities are not allowed to pick their own topics
a.why: Many people see climate change as an urgent problem, and problems seen as urgent are more likely to attract research money. Other topics are not fully explained, and science studies many kinds of problems, not just those linked to the air.
a.clue: Think about what people want solved.

b.q: A town has many people with a common lung disease. Its state government offers extra funds for lung disease research. What best explains this decision?
opts: Many people there are ill and want better treatments
Lung disease is simpler to study than other diseases
Scientists were told which results they must find
Only charities, not governments, can fund research
b.why: Many people in the town are ill, so better treatments are wanted, and that helped steer the funding choice. The decision is about which topic to fund, not which results to find, and governments can fund research as well as charities.
b.clue: Think about who the funding is meant to help.

a.q: A lot of research money goes into ways of cutting greenhouse gas emissions. What best explains this?
opts: Many people see climate change as a problem to solve
Emissions are easier to measure than other topics
Climate research costs less than most other research
Funders pick topics at random to share out their money
a.why: Society's needs and values steer funding, and many people see climate change as an urgent problem that needs solving. The card does not link funding to how cheap or easy a topic is, and funding choices are made on purpose, not at random.
a.clue: Whose concerns does the funding respond to?

b.q: Many people in a country town have a common lung disease. The state government then offers extra money for lung disease research. What best explains this choice?
opts: Many people there are ill and want better treatments
Lung disease is simpler to study than other diseases
The disease is rare, so little is known about it yet
Lung research costs less than other medical research
b.why: Many people in the town are ill, so better treatments are needed, and that need helped steer the funding. The disease is common there, not rare, and nothing in the case suggests lung research is simpler or cheaper.
b.clue: Who in the town would gain from the research?
